title.en: Call by Value and Call by Reference
title.bn: মান ও অ্যাড্রেস দিয়ে ফাংশন কল

summary.en: Distinguish copied arguments from changes made through copied pointers.
summary.bn: C-তে মানের কপি যায়; পয়েন্টারের কপি দিয়ে কলারের ভেরিয়েবল কীভাবে বদলায় তা বোঝো।

keywords: call by value and call by reference

notes: Pass-by-value is unchanged through C23; C has no built-in reference parameter type.

sections.title: A copied address can still reach the original
Read the address and the object separately
Compare the two swaps one assignment at a time
Match each operation to the intended object
Make updates visible at the call
Reference terminology does not change the language rule

examples.title: A swap that changes only copies
examples.explanationHtml: The helper prints 30 12, while main still prints 12 30. Both parameters were separate int objects.

examples.title: Swap caller variables through their addresses
examples.explanationHtml: Dereferencing the copied addresses reaches main variables. The original objects now hold 30 and 12.

examples.title: Reassigning a pointer parameter is local
examples.explanationHtml: The local pointer is redirected, so other becomes 25. The caller pointer still selects original, whose value remains 7.

examples.title: Check an optional output address
examples.explanationHtml: The first call succeeds and leaves value equal to 5. A null pointer is rejected before dereferencing it.

practice.title: Order two scores in place
practice.statementHtml: Read two scores from 0 to 100. Use a pointer helper to put the smaller first. Print Scores: before input, then the ordered pair.
hints: Only swap when the first value is greater.

practice.title: Transfer a limited balance
practice.statementHtml: Read source balance, destination balance and amount, each from 0 to 1000. A pointer helper transfers the amount only if the source can afford it. Print Balances and amount: before input, then success (0 or 1), source and destination.
hints: Check the balance before either write.

practice.title: Rotate three rolls
practice.statementHtml: Read three integers from 0 to 100. Through three pointers, move old third to first, old first to second, and old second to third. Print Rolls: before input, then the three new values.
hints: Save the third value before overwriting it.

practice.title: Swap an object with itself safely
practice.statementHtml: Read one integer from -100 to 100. Call swap with its address twice. Print Number: before input, then its value.
hints: An ordinary temporary-based swap works even when the pointers are equal.

quiz.prompt: What is copied when an int pointer is passed to a function?
quiz.explanation: C copies pointer values just as it copies integer values. The copied pointer can still select shared storage.

quiz.prompt: Why does swap_copies(int a, int b) leave caller variables unchanged?
options: Only separate parameter objects are assigned
C forbids changes inside every helper
The two values must be equal
quiz.explanation: The value arguments initialize local copies. Assignments target those copies.

quiz.prompt: A parameter copy is incremented. Which caller value survives?
quiz.explanation: The helper prints its copy as nine. The original object remains eight.

quiz.prompt: Which statement updates the int selected by pointer p?
quiz.explanation: Dereferencing selects the target object. Assigning p itself would change the pointer rather than the int.

quiz.prompt: Does p != NULL prove that p points to a live writable int?
options: Yes, NULL is the only invalid pointer
Yes, if p has pointer type
Only when sizeof int is four
No, non-null pointers can still be invalid
quiz.explanation: A null check removes one invalid case. Lifetime, provenance, type and writability still matter.

quiz.prompt: A copied pointer writes into a caller int. Which value is then printed?
quiz.explanation: Dereferencing reaches the original int, so eight becomes eleven.

quiz.prompt: What does assigning p = other inside an int-pointer helper change?
options: Every pointer to the former target
quiz.explanation: The parameter is a copied pointer. Changing it redirects only that local copy.

quiz.prompt: Why save a temporary before the first swap write?
options: The old first value is still needed for the second write
It extends both variables to static duration
quiz.explanation: Without a saved value, the first assignment destroys data needed later.

quiz.prompt: Retargeting a local pointer selects b. What happens to a and b?
quiz.explanation: Only b is written after the local p is changed to q.

quiz.prompt: What happens when the shown temporary-based swap receives one address twice?
options: It creates two new caller objects
quiz.explanation: Both targets are the same live object. Saving and restoring its value is safe for this implementation.

quiz.prompt: What does const int *input prevent inside a helper?
options: Any other code changing the object
Writing the selected int through input
quiz.explanation: The const-qualified access path is read-only for the int. It does not make every alias immutable.

keyPoints.en: C passes every argument by value, including pointers.
keyPoints.bn: C সব আর্গুমেন্টের মান কপি করে, পয়েন্টারের মানও।

keyPoints.en: Assigning to an int parameter changes only the copy.
keyPoints.bn: int প্যারামিটার বদলালে শুধু কপিটি বদলায়।

keyPoints.en: The address operator obtains the location of an object.
Dereferencing a valid pointer accesses its target object.
keyPoints.bn: বৈধ পয়েন্টার ডিরেফারেন্স করলে মূল ভেরিয়েবল পাওয়া যায়।

keyPoints.en: A pointer swap needs a temporary to preserve one value.
keyPoints.bn: পয়েন্টার দিয়ে swap করতেও একটি মান সাময়িকভাবে রাখতে হয়।

keyPoints.en: Pointer targets must remain alive throughout the call.
keyPoints.bn: ফাংশন চলাকালে পয়েন্টারের মূল ভেরিয়েবলটি বেঁচে থাকতে হবে।

examQuestions.question: Explain why swapping two int parameters fails to swap caller variables, while pointer parameters can succeed.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The int parameters are separate copied objects. Pointer parameters are also copied, but their values identify the original writable caller objects. Starred assignments write those targets. A temporary preserves the first original value before it is overwritten.

#include <stdio.h>

void change(int value)
{
    value++;
    printf("inside:%d\n", value);
}

int main(void)
{
    int value = 8;
    change(value);
    printf("%d\n", value);
    return 0;
}

inside:9
8

The helper prints its copy as nine. The original object remains eight.

examQuestions.question: Read one integer from -100 to 100. Call swap with its address twice. Print Number: before input, then its value.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
#include <stdio.h>

void swap(int *a, int *b)
{
    int temporary = *a;
    *a = *b;
    *b = temporary;
}

int main(void)
{
    int value;
    puts("Number:");
    if (scanf("%d", &value) != 1 || value < -100 || value > 100) {
        return 1;
    }
    swap(&value, &value);
    printf("%d\n", value);
    return 0;
}

An ordinary temporary-based swap works even when the pointers are equal.

For input -100, the program prints:

Number:
-100
